title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash lets you build with more control
gist: Google's Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash upgrades generative video with longer scene extension, first/last-frame control, cheap 360p drafting, and 4K upscaling, distributed simultaneously through Google AI Studio, the Enterprise Agent Platform, Google Flow, and the Gemini app -- and is already embedded by third parties including Adobe, Figma, GMI Cloud, and even would-be competitor Runway.

insights.claim: Omni 1.1 Flash can analyze up to 10 seconds of prior video context when extending a scene, versus previous models that referenced only the final second, allowing extension in 10-second increments up to a cumulative 40 seconds total.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: A 10x jump in context window for video continuity (1s to 10s) directly improves narrative and visual consistency, a key benchmark investors should track against rival video models (e.g., other labs' scene-extension limits) since the 40-second cumulative cap still bounds how long a fully AI-generated continuous narrative can currently run.
insights.quote: With Omni 1.1, the model can now analyze up to 10 seconds of prior context — a leap from previous models that only referenced the final second.

insights.claim: Omni 1.1 Flash supports specifying first and last frames so the model generates continuous video between two keyframes, targeting complex camera orbits, zoom transitions, and seamless loops.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Keyframe-constrained generation gives professional editors more deterministic creative control than pure text-to-video, closing a gap with traditional video-production tools and making the model more usable in professional post-production pipelines rather than only novelty generation.
insights.quote: Achieve smooth transitions and camera movements by specifying the starting and ending frames of a shot.

insights.claim: Developers can generate lightweight 360p preview drafts up to 60% faster and at roughly a third of the cost compared to Omni 1.1's standard 720p resolution.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Tiered pricing by resolution (cheap 360p drafts, priced-up 720p standard, premium 4K upscale) is a metered-compute monetization structure similar to cloud infrastructure pricing, letting Google capture more revenue per project as users move from prototyping to final output, and lowering the cost barrier for high-volume experimentation which could drive usage growth.
insights.quote: Generate lightweight previews in 360p resolution up to 60% faster* and at a third of the cost compared to Omni 1.1’s standard 720p resolution.

insights.claim: Omni 1.1 Flash can upscale generated video to 1080p or 4K resolution for professional production use.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: 4K output moves Google's video model from consumer-novelty quality toward broadcast/production-grade deliverables, widening the addressable market to professional studios and ad agencies that require high-resolution final assets.
insights.quote: Generate polished, high-resolution 1080p or 4K outputs that are ready for professional production with Omni 1.1.

insights.claim: Omni 1.1 Flash accepts up to three seconds of reference video as multimodal input to maintain visual context and character consistency across generations, e.g. transposing dance moves from reference clips onto new characters in a single continuous shot.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Character/identity consistency has been a well-known weakness of generative video models; solving it via reference-video conditioning is a competitive technical differentiator relevant to any studio or brand needing consistent characters across a campaign or series.
insights.quote: Reference up to three seconds of video when crafting your scene, allowing you to maintain visual context and character consistency based on video references.
insights.locator: "Add video references in your multimodal input" section

insights.claim: Omni 1.1 Flash is being distributed simultaneously through Google AI Studio and the Gemini API for developers, the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API for enterprises, Google Flow for all Google AI Plus/Pro/Ultra subscribers globally, and the Gemini app (scene extension only) for the same subscriber tiers.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Simultaneously monetizing the same underlying model through developer API fees, enterprise platform contracts, and consumer subscription tiers (Plus/Pro/Ultra) diversifies Google's revenue capture from a single model asset across B2D, B2B, and B2C channels at once.
insights.quote: Omni 1.1 is also available to all Google AI Plus, Pro and Ultra subscribers globally in Google Flow, starting today.
insights.locator: "Build with Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash Today" section

insights.claim: Adobe has integrated Gemini Omni Flash into Adobe Firefly's video editing capabilities.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Adobe embedding a Google model inside Firefly -- rather than relying solely on Adobe's own Firefly video models -- signals that even major creative-software incumbents are willing to be multi-model, which commoditizes the underlying model layer and shifts competitive value toward the application/workflow layer.
insights.quote: Adobe integrated Gemini Omni Flash into Adobe Firefly.
insights.locator: "See how customers are putting Omni Flash in production" section

insights.claim: Figma's Creative Director for Weave, Itay Schiff, describes Gemini Omni Flash as one of the strongest video models available in Figma Weave, citing its extensions, reference material handling, and 4K resolution as taking teams from generating videos to directing them.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Design-tool platforms like Figma positioning Gemini as a best-in-class embedded video engine expands Google's reach into the creative-professional workflow market without Google having to own the design-tool interface itself.
insights.quote: Gemini Omni Flash is one of the strongest video models available in Figma Weave, where the canvas helps creative teams build on every generation — attaching references, branching different versions, and shaping something unique.

insights.claim: GMI Cloud's VP of Marketing, Louisa Guo, says Omni Flash's output accuracy under scrutiny has made AI video viable for customers producing educational and explanatory content -- a segment that previously could not rely on AI video.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: If accuracy/reliability genuinely clears the bar for educational content (a use case with low tolerance for visual or factual errors), this expands Omni's addressable market beyond entertainment/marketing into e-learning and explainer-video production, a segment previously underserved by generative video.
insights.quote: Omni has made AI video viable for a segment that previously couldn’t rely on it.

insights.claim: Runway's Chief Creative Officer, Jamie Umpherson, states that Omni Flash fits naturally into Runway's own product workflow, letting users move quickly between ideas starting from a prompt, image, or video.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Runway, a specialist generative-video company with its own foundation models, choosing to integrate a rival's model (Gemini Omni) into its product is a notable signal that model quality/cost leadership is shifting toward large labs like Google DeepMind, and that even model-native competitors are hedging by becoming multi-model front-ends rather than betting solely on proprietary models -- a dynamic worth watching for how it pressures standalone video-model startups' differentiation and pricing power.
insights.quote: Omni Flash fits naturally into how people already use Runway: start with a prompt, an image or a video, then generate or edit from there.

insights.claim: Developers are building tools using Omni's first/last-frame and full-context reasoning to generate realistic camera-move transitions between a dropped-in first and last frame using presets or a prompt box.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: This points toward a new category of consumer/prosumer creative apps built as thin front-ends over Omni's API, which could become an ecosystem Google can monetize via API usage without building the end-user product itself.
insights.quote: you can drop in a first and last frame, generate the transition between them with presets or a prompt box because of Omni's full-context reasoning enabling you to get camera moves that read as real.
insights.locator: "Inspiring concepts for what you can build" section

insights.claim: One showcased application uses Omni to generate aspirational real-estate walkthrough videos that move through rooms without adding furniture or details that don't exist in the actual property.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: Real estate marketing is a concrete vertical where accurate (non-hallucinated) AI video generation has commercial value, suggesting proptech and real-estate marketing tools are a plausible near-term adoption vector for Omni-based products.
insights.quote: It shows the home in an aspirational state, At the perfect time of day. It adds no furniture or details that don’t exist.
insights.locator: "Inspiring concepts for what you can build" section

insights.claim: A featured "Draft Room" workflow pattern generates 3-4 draft variations of a video in cheap 360p, varying one variable at a time, so creators can compare options side by side before committing to a final higher-resolution render.
insights.speaker: Anish Nangia
insights.so_what: This structured cheap-iterate-then-expensive-finalize workflow is the practical payoff of the tiered 360p/720p/4K pricing, and is a template other AI media companies may replicate to reduce iteration cost for end users while preserving upsell revenue at the final-render stage.
insights.quote: The Draft Room makes that exploration cheap and structured: generate 3-4 draft variations in 360p, varying one thing at a time and compare them side by side.
insights.locator: "Inspiring concepts for what you can build" section
